question: What is the correct order of organisation in the human body?
What is the role of bile in digestion?
options: It digests proteins into amino acids
It emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid
It breaks down starch into sugars
It absorbs water from undigested food
correct: It emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid

question: Which enzyme breaks down starch?
What happens to an enzyme when it is denatured?
options: Its active site changes shape permanently
correct: Its active site changes shape permanently

question: Where is bile produced?
Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body?
Which chambers of the heart pump blood out to the lungs and body?
What is the function of valves in the heart?
options: To pump blood around the body
To prevent the backflow of blood
To carry oxygen to heart muscle
correct: To prevent the backflow of blood

question: Which blood vessel has the thickest walls?
What is a malignant tumour?
options: A tumour that stays in one place and does not spread
A tumour that spreads to other parts of the body
A tumour caused only by smoking
A tumour that is always fatal
correct: A tumour that spreads to other parts of the body

question: Which component of blood carries oxygen around the body?
Which tissue transports water and mineral ions up the plant?
What controls the opening and closing of stomata?
What causes coronary heart disease?
options: A viral infection of the heart muscle
A build-up of fatty plaques in the coronary arteries
A lack of red blood cells
Damage to the heart valves by bacteria
correct: A build-up of fatty plaques in the coronary arteries

question: What do villi do in the small intestine?
options: Increase the surface area for absorption
correct: Increase the surface area for absorption

question: An enzyme's shape is changed permanently by high temperatures. This is called being __________.
The enzyme __________ breaks down proteins into amino acids.
Bile is produced by the __________ and stored in the gall bladder.
The __________ are the upper chambers of the heart that receive blood.
Blood vessels called __________ carry blood away from the heart.
The liquid part of blood that carries dissolved substances is called __________.
The loss of water vapour from plant leaves through the stomata is called __________.
__________ tissue transports dissolved sugars from leaves to the rest of the plant.
A tumour that spreads to other parts of the body is described as __________.
The wave-like muscular contractions that move food along the digestive system are called __________.
Match each enzyme to the food molecule it breaks down.

pairs.definition: Breaks down proteins into amino acids
Breaks down lipids into fatty acids and glycerol

question: Match each blood vessel to its correct description.

pairs.definition: Carries blood away from the heart, thick muscular walls, no valves
Carries blood towards the heart, thin walls, has valves
One cell thick, site of exchange between blood and tissues

question: Match each digestive organ to its function.

pairs.definition: Produces protease and hydrochloric acid to digest proteins
Produces amylase, protease and lipase enzymes
Main site of digestion and absorption of nutrients
Absorbs water from undigested food to form faeces

question: Match each plant tissue to its function.

pairs.definition: Transports water and mineral ions from roots to leaves
Transports dissolved sugars from leaves to the rest of the plant
Control the opening and closing of stomata
Packed with chloroplasts — main site of photosynthesis in the leaf

question: Match each blood component to its function.

pairs.definition: Carry oxygen around the body using haemoglobin
Help blood to clot at a wound
Liquid that carries dissolved nutrients, hormones and waste

question: State what is meant by the term enzyme.
mark_scheme: A biological catalyst (1) that speeds up chemical reactions without being used up (1) — accept either point.

question: Name the blood vessel that supplies the heart muscle with oxygenated blood.
mark_scheme: Coronary artery (1).

question: State the difference between a benign and a malignant tumour.
mark_scheme: Benign tumour stays in one place / does not spread (1); malignant tumour spreads to other parts of the body (1) — accept either point for 1 mark.

question: State the function of stomata in a leaf.
mark_scheme: Allow gas exchange (1) / allow water vapour to escape during transpiration (1) — accept either.

question: Explain why enzymes are described as specific.
mark_scheme: Each enzyme has a specific active site (1); only one substrate fits the active site — lock and key model (1); so each enzyme only catalyses one type of reaction (1) — any two.

question: Explain why the small intestine is well adapted for absorption.
mark_scheme: Villi increase the surface area (1); villi have a good blood supply to maintain a concentration gradient (1); villi have thin walls for a short diffusion distance (1) — any two.

question: Describe the function of arteries and veins.
mark_scheme: Arteries carry blood away from the heart (1); veins carry blood towards the heart (1); arteries have thick muscular walls (1); veins have valves to prevent backflow (1) — any two.

question: Explain how guard cells control the opening of stomata.
mark_scheme: When guard cells gain water they become turgid and change shape (1); this opens the stomata (1); when they lose water they become flaccid and stomata close (1) — any two.

question: Explain how a stent is used to treat coronary heart disease.
mark_scheme: A stent is a metal mesh tube (1); inserted into a narrowed coronary artery (1); it holds the artery open / restores blood flow to the heart muscle (1) — any two.

question: Explain the role of bile in the digestion of fats.
mark_scheme: Bile is produced in the liver (1); stored in the gall bladder (1); emulsifies fats — breaks large fat droplets into smaller ones (1); increases surface area for lipase to work (1); bile is alkaline and neutralises stomach acid (1) — any three.

question: Describe the structure and function of capillaries.
mark_scheme: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels (1); walls are one cell thick (1); short diffusion distance for exchange of substances (1); large network provides large surface area (1); substances such as oxygen and glucose diffuse into tissues (1) — any three.

question: Explain how increasing temperature affects enzyme activity, including what happens above the optimum temperature.
mark_scheme: Increasing temperature increases rate of reaction (1); more enzyme-substrate collisions (1); above optimum temperature the enzyme denatures (1); active site changes shape (1); substrate no longer fits (1) — any three.

question: Explain what transpiration is and describe the factors that affect its rate.
mark_scheme: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves through stomata (1); light intensity — more light increases rate (1); temperature — higher temperature increases rate (1); humidity — lower humidity increases rate (1); wind speed — more wind increases rate (1) — any three.

question: Explain how the digestive system breaks down a meal containing starch, protein and fat, naming the enzymes involved and where they act.
mark_scheme: Amylase breaks down starch in the mouth and small intestine (1); protease breaks down proteins in the stomach and small intestine (1); lipase breaks down fats in the small intestine (1); bile emulsifies fats increasing surface area for lipase (1); products absorbed in the small intestine (1) — any four.

question: Describe the double circulation of blood in the human body, including the role of the heart.
mark_scheme: Blood travels from the heart to the lungs to pick up oxygen (1); returns to the heart (1); then pumped to the rest of the body (1); heart has four chambers — two atria and two ventricles (1); left side pumps oxygenated blood to body (1); right side pumps deoxygenated blood to lungs (1) — any four.

question: Evaluate the use of statins and stents as treatments for coronary heart disease.
mark_scheme: Statins lower cholesterol levels (1); reduce risk of fatty plaques forming (1); must be taken long-term / side effects possible (1); stents hold arteries open physically (1); immediate effect (1); risk of surgery / blood clots (1); statins are a preventive treatment, stents are a cure (1) — any four.

question: Explain what cancer is and describe the difference between benign and malignant tumours. Include risk factors for cancer in your answer.
mark_scheme: Cancer is uncontrolled cell division (1); benign tumour stays in one place (1); malignant tumour spreads to other tissues / metastasis (1); risk factors include smoking / UV radiation / viral infections / inherited genes (1); lifestyle factors can increase or decrease risk (1) — any four.

question: Explain how the structure of the small intestine is adapted to maximise the absorption of digested food molecules.
mark_scheme: Villi increase the surface area for absorption (1); microvilli on villi further increase surface area (1); villi have a rich blood supply — maintains concentration gradient (1); walls are one cell thick — short diffusion distance (1); large intestine absorbs water (1); lacteals in villi absorb fatty acids and glycerol (1) — any five.

question: A patient is diagnosed with coronary heart disease. Explain what causes this condition, the symptoms it produces, and the treatments available.
mark_scheme: Fatty plaques build up in the coronary arteries (1); arteries become narrowed (1); blood flow to heart muscle is restricted (1); heart muscle receives less oxygen (1); symptoms include chest pain / angina / heart attack (1); treatments: statins lower cholesterol (1); stents hold arteries open (1); bypass surgery uses another blood vessel to go around the blockage (1) — any six.

question: Evaluate the lifestyle changes and medical treatments available to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. In your answer, refer to both advantages and disadvantages.
mark_scheme: Lifestyle: healthy diet reduces cholesterol (1); exercise strengthens heart muscle (1); stopping smoking reduces risk (1); no side effects from lifestyle changes (1); requires willpower and long-term commitment (1). Medical: statins reduce cholesterol effectively (1); may have side effects (1); stents give immediate relief (1); surgery carries risk (1); medical treatments may be needed when lifestyle changes are insufficient (1) — any six.
